sheet-74-1.description: The main map of the single Oceanport sheet, sheet 74 of the New Jersey Coast volume 1, drawn at 60 ft to an inch with north towards the upper left. It covers the centre of the village of Oceanport between the Shrewsbury River on the west and Pemberton on the east, from the fork at the top of the sheet, where the Road to Red Bank leaves Main to the north-west and a road to Long Branch curves away to the north-east, down to Mill at the foot of the sheet. Main runs the length of the sheet with a 12 inch water pipe down it; Arcania crosses from Main to Pemberton at mid-sheet, and Maiden Lane runs south from Arcania to the middle of the block. A private road leads west from Main towards the river in the lower half. The village is almost wholly residential: rows of frame dwellings on narrow lots numbered 201 to 244 along Main and 301 to 338 along Pemberton, with stables, sheds and an ice house behind them, and a few stores near the fork. Public buildings are few: a hose cart and hook and ladder truck house at the top of the sheet north of the Road to Red Bank, the M.E. Church on the east side of Main near Mill, and hydrants at the corners of Main with Arcania and Mill. A 36 inch supply pipe to Long Branch is drawn along the Road to Red Bank and the road to Long Branch. A large open block north of Arcania between Main and Pemberton carries the village name and a note on the fire protection: population 600, no steam and no hand engine, one independent hose cart, one hook and ladder truck, water from Long Branch, prevailing wind west. The blank area at the top left is covered by the inset of part 2.
notes: Arcania is today Arcana Avenue; Maiden Lane is Trinity Place; Mill is Center Street; Main is Main Street; Pemberton is Pemberton Avenue.

The Road to Red Bank corresponds to the north-west leg of today's Oceanport Avenue and the road to Long Branch to East Main Street; the fork has been rebuilt, and the modern node of Main Street, East Main Street and Oceanport Avenue lies about 15 m east of the drawn fork, so it was not used as control.
Today's Oceanport Avenue south-east of the fork, across the open block north of Arcania, did not exist; its junction with Pemberton Avenue was excluded.
Control: five detected street junctions and four hand-picked parcel block corners (lot lines along Pemberton near the top of the sheet and along the west side of Main).
Faint handwritten lettering runs up the right-hand margin; it could not be read.

Sheet 74 of New Jersey Coast vol. 1, Oceanport, scale 60 ft to an inch, north to the upper left (true about -38 deg). Main map: Main, Arcania (Arcana Avenue), Maiden Lane (Trinity Place), Mill (Center Street), Pemberton, Rd. to Red Bank and the road to Long Branch at the top; Shrewsbury River on the west. Part 2: boxed inset at the top left, drawn at about -70 deg, showing Main (now East Main Street) at Pemberton with the Park Hotel, off the top of the main map. Part 1: 5 detected junctions plus 4 parcel block corners; the modern Main/East Main/Oceanport Avenue node (about 15 m east of the drawn fork) and the modern Oceanport Avenue/Pemberton junction (street not yet built) are excluded. Part 2 placed from two lot-line points carried from part 1 (low confidence).

sheet-74-2.description: A boxed inset in the top left corner of the Oceanport sheet (sheet 74 of the New Jersey Coast volume 1), drawn at the same scale of 60 ft to an inch but turned so that north points almost to the left. It shows ground that lies just beyond the top of the main map: the junction of Main, here the road to Long Branch that is today East Main Street, with Pemberton, which runs in from the right edge of the box and is lettered 30 ft wide. The wedge between the two streets holds the Park Hotel, a two and a half storey frame building with a saloon, together with a wagon shed, an ice house and small outbuildings; the rest of the block is open ground divided into large lots. West of Main, across a dashed street line and a 36 inch supply pipe to Long Branch that runs along the street, are a store, the M.H. Hall, a dwelling and the bank of a creek or river at the left edge of the box. Pemberton carries the note 100 ft to D.H. Block numbers 1 and 2 and the sheet number 74 are repeated in the box. The inset is placed from two lot-line points that it shares with the top edge of the main map along Main, with the scale of the main map and the rotation of the inset's own north arrow, which agrees with the directions of both streets today.
notes: Main in this inset is today East Main Street; Pemberton is Pemberton Avenue.

Placed from two points carried from part 1 (a lot line meeting Main and a meeting of three lot lines, about 100 ft apart, drawn on both) with the scale of part 1 and a rotation of -70 degrees; low confidence away from them.

So placed, the drawn junction of Main and Pemberton lies about 24 m north-north-east of today's East Main Street / Pemberton Avenue node, and the drawn Main about 8 to 10 m north of today's East Main Street; the main map shows the same offset where it draws the street, so East Main Street appears to have been moved south since 1907.
The Park Hotel and its outbuildings no longer stand.
